title: The Best Pass
source_body:
The Best Pass

Dohun was the best basketball player on his school team. Last season, he had scored more than half of the team's points. Whenever he got the ball, he tried to shoot, even when three players were guarding him.

But the team kept losing. In the semifinal game, Dohun missed shot after shot, and the team lost by ten points. After the game, Coach Kim sat down next to him.

"Dohun, you are a great player," she said. "But basketball is not a one-person game. When you have the ball, look around. Your teammates are open."

For the next month, Dohun practiced passing as hard as he had practiced shooting. At first, it felt strange. But slowly, he began to trust his teammates, and they began to trust him.

In the final game of the season, the team was behind by two points with only five seconds left. Dohun got the ball, and everyone expected him to shoot. Instead, he saw Jaewon, who was standing alone at the three-point line, and passed. Jaewon shot, and the ball went in just as the whistle blew.

The team jumped into the air together. Dohun had not scored the winning shot, but he no longer cared. It was the best pass of his life.

variants.advanced:
The Best Pass

Dohun was, without question, the most talented basketball player on his school team. Last season, he had scored more than half of the team's points on his own. Whenever the ball came to him, he attempted a shot, even when he was surrounded by three defenders.

Nevertheless, the team kept losing. In the semifinal, Dohun missed one shot after another, and the team was defeated by ten points. After the game, Coach Kim sat down beside him.

"Dohun, you are a remarkable player," she said. "But basketball is not a one-person game. Whenever you have the ball, look around. Your teammates are often left wide open."

For the following month, Dohun practiced passing as intensely as he had once practiced shooting. At first, it felt unnatural to him. Gradually, however, he learned to rely on his teammates, and they, in turn, came to trust him.

In the final game of the season, the team was trailing by two points with only five seconds remaining. When Dohun received the ball, everyone assumed that he would take the shot. Instead, he spotted Jaewon, who was standing unguarded at the three-point line, and passed. Jaewon shot, and the ball dropped through the net just as the final whistle blew.

The whole team leapt into the air together. Although Dohun had not scored the winning basket, it no longer mattered to him. It was the best pass he had ever made.
variants.prestudy:
The Best Pass

Dohun was indisputably the most gifted basketball player on his school's team. During the previous season, he had single-handedly accounted for more than half of the team's points. Whenever he gained possession of the ball, he would attempt a shot, even when three opponents were closely guarding him.

Despite his individual brilliance, however, the team continued to suffer defeats. In the semifinal, Dohun missed shot after shot, and his team was eliminated by a ten-point margin. After the game, Coach Kim quietly took a seat beside him.

"Dohun, you are an exceptional player," she remarked. "But basketball is not a one-person game. Whenever you have the ball, survey the court. Your teammates are frequently left unguarded."

Throughout the following month, Dohun devoted himself to passing as relentlessly as he had once devoted himself to shooting. Initially, it felt awkward and unfamiliar. Gradually, though, he began to place his trust in his teammates, and they, in turn, began to place their trust in him.

In the season's championship game, the team was trailing by two points with merely five seconds remaining on the clock. When Dohun received the ball, everyone anticipated that he would take the final shot. Instead, he noticed Jaewon, who was positioned alone beyond the three-point line, and delivered a pass. Jaewon released the shot, and the ball swished through the net at the precise moment the buzzer sounded.

The entire team leapt into the air in celebration. Although Dohun had not been the one to score the decisive basket, this no longer mattered to him in the slightest. It was, without a doubt, the finest pass he had ever made.
